questiontext.text:
A student plans to prove a statement about every integer \(n\) by splitting into cases by the remainder on division by {@md@}. The cases listed are [[foreach jj="makelist(j, j, 1, ncases)"]]{@caselist[jj]@}[[if test="is(jj < ncases - 1)"]], [[/if]][[if test="is(jj = ncases - 1)"]] and [[/if]][[/foreach]]. One case is missing.

Write an expression for \(n\) in the missing case, using an integer \(k\). Any correct form is accepted.

\(n =\) [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Every integer leaves exactly one of the remainders \(0, 1, \ldots, {@md-1@}\) on division by {@md@}, so a split by remainders needs all {@md@} of them. The list has remainders [[foreach jj="makelist(j, j, 1, ncases)"]]{@listed[jj]@}[[if test="is(jj < ncases - 1)"]], [[/if]][[if test="is(jj = ncases - 1)"]] and [[/if]][[/foreach]]; remainder {@rmiss@} is missing, so the missing case is \(n = {@ta1@}\).

Other correct forms include \(n = {@talt1@}\) and \(n = {@talt2@}\): as \(k\) runs through all the integers, each gives exactly the same integers. An expression such as {@dmult@} is not enough: it gives only some of them (it never gives {@md + rmiss@}).

questiondescription.text: This question is based on the divisibility of integers (Tips, item 3), pp. 15-16, in Section 5 of Bokhove, C., Thoma, A., Gammack, D., Yu, L. H. S., Roberts, S. and Downey, F., Thinking about Proof, 1st edition, University of Southampton, 2022.

node.description: Diagnostic: coefficient of k must be the modulus

falsefeedback.text: Your expression is {@sa@}. The coefficient of \(k\) must be {@md@} (or {@-md@}). Then, as \(k\) runs through all the integers, the expression gives every integer with one particular remainder on division by {@md@}, and no others. With coefficient {@ca@} it does not.

node.description: Diagnostic: right remainder, or a case already listed

falsefeedback.text: Your expression gives the integers with remainder {@rgot@} on division by {@md@}, and that case is already in the list. Which of the remainders \(0, 1, \ldots, {@md-1@}\) does not appear?

qtest.description: Invalid: a number with no k
